verses.verse:
अभ्यासस्तालयोगेन स्वराणाम् हि महाफलः।
कालं समं विभाज्याथ स्वराः साध्या मुहुर्मुहुः।९६।
verses.text: Practice of the notes joined with tāla (metric cycle) bears great fruit; then, dividing time into equal parts, the notes should be practised again and again.

commentary.text: Before practising the notes with tāla (metric cycle), it is necessary to practise the laya (tempo) connected with tāla. The regular movement of anything is called laya. Just as the hand of a clock ticks at regular moments, so if the clap of our hand goes at regular times, we call it laya. Now if we count along with that clap, it will be called a laya of counting equal to the clap.
And if we divide the moment of each clap into two equal parts and say two counts in each clap, the laya (tempo) of the counting will be twice that of the clap, for example —

In the same way, if the moment of the clap is divided into three or four equal parts and as many counts are said, the laya (tempo) of that counting will be called threefold or fourfold. Now if sargam is said in place of the counting, the sargam too will be said to have the same kind of laya. For example —

In the way shown above, while clapping with the hands, one should recite the sargam with the mouth in different layas (tempos). Keep in mind that while doing double [speed] with the mouth, the speed of the hand does not also start to increase. Then, by marking the clap with the foot, the ability to play the sargam on the bānsurī too will develop. Just as a capable witness (a guru) is needed for knowledge of svara, so a witness is needed for knowledge of laya too, one who can turn the incorrect into correct.
